# google_vertex_ai_semantic_governance_policy

A Semantic Governance Policy governs an AI agent's actions and tool execution
using natural language constraints. A policy requires an active
SemanticGovernancePolicyEngine (`google_vertex_ai_semantic_governance_policy_engine`)
in the same project and region.


To get more information about SemanticGovernancePolicy, see:

* [API documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.semanticGovernancePolicies)
* How-to Guides
    * [Semantic governance overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/policies/semantic-governance-overview)

## Example Usage - Vertex Ai Semantic Governance Policy Basic


```hcl
resource "google_vertex_ai_semantic_governance_policy_engine" "sgpe" {
  region  = "us-central1"
}

resource "google_vertex_ai_reasoning_engine" "agent" {
  display_name = "example-agent"
  region       = "us-central1"

  spec {
    identity_type = "AGENT_IDENTITY"
  }
}

resource "time_sleep" "wait_for_ingestion" {
  depends_on      = [google_vertex_ai_reasoning_engine.agent]
  create_duration = "120s"
}

data "google_agent_registry_agent" "agent" {
  location   = "us-central1"
  filter     = "displayName=\"${google_vertex_ai_reasoning_engine.agent.display_name}\""
  depends_on = [time_sleep.wait_for_ingestion]
}

resource "google_vertex_ai_semantic_governance_policy" "policy" {
  semantic_governance_policy_id = "example-policy"
  region                        = "us-central1"
  natural_language_constraint   = "Do not access internal developer endpoints"
  agent                         = data.google_agent_registry_agent.agent.id

  depends_on = [google_vertex_ai_semantic_governance_policy_engine.sgpe]
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `natural_language_constraint` -
  (Required)
  The natural language constraint of the SemanticGovernancePolicy.

* `agent` -
  (Required)
  The name of the agent in Agent Registry that is affected by this policy.

* `semantic_governance_policy_id` -
  (Required)
  The ID of the SemanticGovernancePolicy, which will become the final component of the resource name.
  This value may be up to 63 characters, and valid characters are [a-z0-9-]. The first character cannot be a number or hyphen. The last character must be a letter or a number.


* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  The user-defined name of the SemanticGovernancePolicy.

* `description` -
  (Optional)
  The description of the SemanticGovernancePolicy.

* `mcp_tools` -
  (Optional)
  The McpTools that are affected by this policy.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_mcp_tools).

* `agent_response_customization` -
  (Optional)
  Settings for customizing the agent's response to end users when this policy is evaluated.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_agent_response_customization).

* `region` -
  (Optional)
  The region of the SemanticGovernancePolicy, e.g. 'us-central1'.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_mcp_tools"></a>The `mcp_tools` block supports:

* `mcp_server` -
  (Required)
  The resource name of the McpServer in Agent Registry that is affected by this policy.
  Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/mcpServers/{mcpServer}`

* `tools` -
  (Required)
  The resource names of the McpTools used by the Agent that is affected by this policy.
  At least one tool must be listed.

<a name="nested_agent_response_customization"></a>The `agent_response_customization` block supports:

* `denial_message` -
  (Optional)
  Custom message shown to the end user when the policy check results in a denial. Use this
  to explain the rationale to the user. Max 1000 characters.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/semanticGovernancePolicies/{{semantic_governance_policy_id}}`

* `name` -
  The resource name of the SemanticGovernancePolicy, in the form
  'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/semanticGovernancePolicies/{semantic_governance_policy}'.

* `create_time` -
  The time the SemanticGovernancePolicy was created, in RFC3339 UTC "Zulu" format.

* `update_time` -
  The time the SemanticGovernancePolicy was last updated, in RFC3339 UTC "Zulu" format.

* `etag` -
  Used to perform consistent read-modify-write transactions.

* `agent_identity` -
  Represents the principal of the agent, used by the Policy Decision Point (PDP) for governance checks.
  For more information, see https://docs.cloud.google.com/agent-builder/agent-engine/agent-identity.
  Format: `principal://TRUST_DOMAIN/NAMESPACE/AGENT_NAME`


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


SemanticGovernancePolicy can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/semanticGovernancePolicies/{{semantic_governance_policy_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{region}}/{{semantic_governance_policy_id}}`
* `{{region}}/{{semantic_governance_policy_id}}`
* `{{semantic_governance_policy_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import SemanticGovernancePolicy using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    semanticGovernancePolicyId = "<-required value->"
    region = "<-optional value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_vertex_ai_semantic_governance_policy.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import SemanticGovernancePolicy using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/semanticGovernancePolicies/{{semantic_governance_policy_id}}"
  to = google_vertex_ai_semantic_governance_policy.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), SemanticGovernancePolicy can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_semantic_governance_policy.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/semanticGovernancePolicies/{{semantic_governance_policy_id}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_semantic_governance_policy.default {{project}}/{{region}}/{{semantic_governance_policy_id}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_semantic_governance_policy.default {{region}}/{{semantic_governance_policy_id}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_semantic_governance_policy.default {{semantic_governance_policy_id}}
```
